source.title: A Stitch in Time Saves Nine: Preserving Policy Compatibility Under Perception Updates in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Yue-Yuan Li; Yi-Fei Xiao; Mingyang Jiang; Xiang Zuo; Song-An Zhang; Ming Yang

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests representation alignment and stitchability in autonomous driving using CKA and downstream task performance, rather than testing convergence with scale using the original claim’s measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layer-wise CKA comparisons (Figure 3), driving performance after perception updates and stitching (Table V), and decoder-task metrics after stitching (Table VII). Cited results from other work and qualitative supervision ratings in Table I are not study results bearing directly on the claim. Table VI measures adaptation efficiency, not representation alignment.
record.test_reason: The study applies standard model stitching (least-squares linear and 1x1 convolutional stitchers fitted on paired latents) and layer-wise CKA in a new setting: BEV perception encoders for end-to-end driving. It measures how well one encoder's latents map onto another's frozen decoder and policy across seed, objective, modality, sensor and domain changes. Its own Table V and VII results bear directly on V4, and on V3 through Case 1 (initialization only).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that task-relevant perception latents across seed, objective, modality, sensor and domain changes admit low-complexity stitching that preserves frozen downstream driving behavior. Linear maps suffice for mild shifts; larger sensor and domain shifts need a convolutional map. They frame it as a task-level hypothesis, not global representational equivalence, and as a far cheaper alternative to retraining (22.18 h to 0.91 h).
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired driving observations and a frozen downstream stack; evaluates least-squares linear and shallow convolutional stitchers by driving behavior and target-decoder task metrics. Adds CKA analysis and does not test global representational equivalence. The paper presents this as model stitching, a close but task-specific application.
record.method_sensitivity: Stitching performance varies with the update condition and mapping capacity: linear stitching is effective for mild shifts but less effective for the larger sensor shift and cross-domain setting; convolutional stitching performs better in those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise CKA between perception models differing in objective (VAE vs AE), modality or camera count is described as higher in deeper layers under shared supervision. It is figure-only, with no values and no scale dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models trained with the same supervisory signal converge in deeper layers, even when objective, modality or sensor setup differ.

record.code_released: https://github.com/SCP-CN-001/model-stitching (stated to be open-sourced upon paper acceptance)
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the alignment or driving metrics. Evaluation is limited to the stated autonomous-driving models, datasets, and scenario; it does not establish scale-dependent convergence or broad cross-modal generality. Figure 3 provides qualitative CKA descriptions without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table V Route Completion (RC) values are omitted because Driving Score is recorded as the primary driving-performance measure and the two are reported together. Table VII source-native decoder values are omitted; target-native references are retained in the baseline fields. Table VI efficiency measures are not representation-alignment results.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. Models are small task-specific BEV encoders.
No vision-language models or image-caption pairs.
No unit-level or basis-level matching. The seed evidence is one model pair (Case 1) plus qualitative CKA figures.
No relative representations and no mapping without paired data; only paired linear and 1x1-conv stitchers at the latent interface.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Only CKA is used; there is no comparison of similarity measures or their settings.
No test of plateau or of the causes of alignment (shared data or objective vs a common model of reality).

missing.what: No-shift reference driving performance (RC 100.0, DS 98.58). This is the proper target reference for the stitching driving scores.

Source models' in-domain performance (mIoU 0.501, mAP@50 0.466) and their degraded native-decoder scores on CARLA 2 (0.178, 0.011). These show the cross-domain stitching gains relative to the source's own transfer.
missing.locator: Table VII source column; Section IV-B.3 text

record.verdict_notes: The convolutional stitcher is a 1x1 conv plus BN, trained with the task loss through the frozen decoder. It is therefore task-supervised rather than a pure representation map, which weakens its reading as pure representational interchangeability. Retraining and fine-tuning rows are adaptation comparators, not alignment evidence. All results come from a single CARLA scenario with no uncertainty estimates. The CKA evidence is qualitative only.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no test of convergence across independently trained models varying architecture, objective, data, and scale together.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.

Tests representational similarity across initialization in the driving setting, but does not establish recurrence of particular units or exact feature identities, nor test all the claimed shared-subspace properties.
Tests paired-observation linear and convolutional stitching for a fixed downstream driving stack. Does not test stitching through layer splicing, relative representations, or without paired data.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.
Does not compare similarity measures, settings such as number of neighbours, or in-distribution and out-of-distribution similarity estimates. It varies update conditions, not the similarity metric.

The paper studies task-relevant stitchability under specified supervision and data conditions, but does not isolate whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause alignment, or measure a general alignment plateau.
